tex_content.html:
For each finite $r$ there is $C(r)<\infty $ such that every based three-dimensional $\kappa $-solution with $R(p,0)=1$ satisfies $R(q,0)\leq C(r)$ on $B(p,0,r)$.
Proof

↗ prop:asymptotic-scalar-curvature-infinite ↗ cor:volume-bound-implies-curvature-bound ↗ cor:three-dimensional-asymptotic-soliton-bounded-curvature \sketch

Choose the closest $q$ to $p$ with $d_0(p,q)^2R(q,0)=1$, and write $d=d_0(p,q)$, $Q=R(q,0)$. Claims 7 and 30 give a universal upper bound for $Q$ and for $R/Q$ on $B(q,2d)$. Claim 30 therefore provides a universal ball about $p$ with uniform curvature bound. Non-collapsing gives a fixed volume lower bound there, and Corollary 2 propagates the curvature estimate to every fixed ball.

□

\begin{claim} \end{claim}[Universal curvature ratio bound near $q$]
